title: Faba bean gall on faba bean

Header: Faba bean gall on faba bean
Olpidium viciae Faba bean gall, Qormid in Amharic language

Prevention: The faba bean gall is a fungal disease, the disease survives in crop debris/residues and in the soil.
Practice crop rotation for at least two seasons with cereals like wheat and barley or
Gomenzar (Brassica carinata) to reduce or eliminate the disease in the soil.
Remove crop debris of the previously diseased pulse crops.
But do not remove debris and residues if no major pest problem is in the field, to help to improve soils.
Avoid or remove excess surface water to prevent the spread of the disease.
Monitoring: Faba bean gall symptoms on leaves and stems from seedlings to pod setting stage every week.
Look for small chlorotic spots, and that then progressively enlarge to become light brown, circular or elliptical rough spots.
Immediately when first symptoms are seen.
Action is too late when small tumor like galls are formed and adjacent galls form huge galls, resulting in rolling up and abnormal growth of leaves.
At the later stage, the galls turn black or brown and a few galls break to form necrotic areas, but action is far too late.
Direct Control: Immediate removal of infected faba bean plant.
Restrictions: No fungicides are registered against this disease yet.
